transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?

Well, my wife actually made the appointment. What finally scared her is that I keep hearing things. I hear water running, and... men whispering inside the walls when nobody’s there. And sometimes I see this dark, wet patch spreading across the hallway. I've gone over and checked it, and it's completely dry, but I still see it. So, that's why I'm here.
About how long have you been hearing these sounds and seeing that patch in the hallway?

It's been about seven months now. It started back during the winter freeze... that's when the house repairs turned into a total mess, and I just couldn't get out from under it all. That's when it all started.
Over these past seven months, have you been feeling persistently down, sad, or depressed?
Yeah, I have. Most days, I wake up and... I just already feel like I've failed at being a husband and a man. It's just this heaviness that sits on me all day, right up until I go to bed.
Have there been any times over these past seven months when you heard the voices or saw the patch, but weren't feeling depressed?

No, they've only happened while I've been feeling this way. Before all the house problems dragged on and I got so... down, I never heard those voices in the walls or saw the wet patch. I never thought the neighbors were tracking me, either. All of that stuff only started happening after I had already stopped caring about my normal life and started feeling like a failure every day. It's like the depression came first, and then the rest of it just followed.

The psychotic symptoms are confined entirely to the period of depression.
